title: Questions and sources, exercise class X — Russia 1917, the dictatorships, European integration

slides.title: Source: Lenin's Decree on Land and Russia's constitutional development 1917–1922
slides.text: THE SOURCE: 'The most equitable settlement of the land question is to be as follows: PRIVATE OWNERSHIP OF LAND IS ABOLISHED FOREVER; land may not be sold, purchased, leased, mortgaged or otherwise alienated. All land — state, crown, monastery, church, factory, entailed, private, public, peasant and the rest — IS CONFISCATED WITHOUT COMPENSATION and becomes THE PROPERTY OF THE WHOLE PEOPLE and passes into the use of all those who work it. […] The right to use the land shall be accorded to all citizens of the Russian state (WITHOUT DISTINCTION OF SEX) who wish to work it BY THEIR OWN LABOUR, with the help of their families or in association, but only so far as they are able to cultivate it. THE HIRING OF WAGE LABOUR IS NOT PERMITTED.' (a speech of 26 October 1917 in the Julian calendar, that is, 8 November in the Gregorian — hence the 'October Revolution' in November.) WHO LENIN WAS AND WHAT HE ACHIEVED: VLADIMIR ILYICH ULYANOV, CALLED LENIN (1870–1924), a lawyer by education, leader of the BOLSHEVIK faction of Russian social democracy; in October 1917, after the coup, he became CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL OF PEOPLE'S COMMISSARS, that is, head of government. THE CONSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT FROM FEBRUARY 1917 TO THE FOUNDING OF THE USSR IN 1922: (1) THE FEBRUARY REVOLUTION (March 1917 Gregorian) — the abdication of Nicholas II, the end of the Romanov monarchy, the emergence of a PROVISIONAL GOVERNMENT alongside the PETROGRAD SOVIET, that is, DUAL POWER. (2) ON 1 SEPTEMBER 1917 Russia is proclaimed a REPUBLIC. (3) THE OCTOBER COUP (7–8 November 1917) — the Bolsheviks take power; the Second Congress of Soviets adopts the DECREE ON PEACE and the DECREE ON LAND. (4) JANUARY 1918 — the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY meets, in which the Bolsheviks have no majority, and is DISPERSED AFTER A SINGLE DAY. (5) JULY 1918 — the CONSTITUTION OF THE RUSSIAN SOVIET FEDERATIVE SOCIALIST REPUBLIC (RSFSR), the first Soviet constitution. (6) 1918–1922 CIVIL WAR and war communism, from 1921 the NEP. (7) ON 30 DECEMBER 1922 — by a treaty between the RSFSR, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian Federation, the UNION OF SOVIET SOCIALIST REPUBLICS COMES INTO BEING; the union constitution follows in 1924.

cards.q: Who was Lenin and what office did he obtain in October 1917?
cards.a: VLADIMIR ILYICH ULYANOV (1870–1924), A LAWYER BY EDUCATION and leader of the BOLSHEVIK faction of Russian social democracy. After the October coup he became CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL OF PEOPLE'S COMMISSARS, that is, head of government.

cards.q: Sketch Russia's constitutional development from February 1917 to the founding of the USSR.
cards.a: THE FEBRUARY REVOLUTION 1917 — the abdication of Nicholas II and the DUAL POWER of the Provisional Government and the Petrograd Soviet. On 1 September 1917 Russia is proclaimed a REPUBLIC. THE OCTOBER COUP (7–8 November 1917) — the decrees on peace and on land. JANUARY 1918 — the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY DISPERSED AFTER A SINGLE DAY. JULY 1918 — the CONSTITUTION OF THE RSFSR. 1918–1922 civil war, from 1921 the NEP. On 30 December 1922 THE FOUNDING OF THE USSR, union constitution 1924.

slides.title: The soviet republic, 'socialist', and property in the USSR
slides.text: WHAT 'SOVIET REPUBLIC' MEANS: SOVIET is Russian for COUNCIL. It is an arrangement in which power derives from COUNCILS OF WORKERS, SOLDIERS AND PEASANTS, elected in workplaces and units, not in territorial constituencies on an equal franchise. Its features: (1) INDIRECT, TIERED ELECTION — the lower soviet elects the higher; (2) A CLASS FRANCHISE — the RSFSR constitution of 1918 excluded 'exploiters' from the vote and weighted workers' votes above peasants'; (3) THE REJECTION OF THE SEPARATION OF POWERS — the soviets are legislative and executive at once, because the separation of powers is regarded as a bourgeois fiction; (4) THE IMPERATIVE MANDATE AND RECALLABILITY of deputies. WHY A 'SOCIALIST' AND NOT A 'COMMUNIST' REPUBLIC: on Marxist theory SOCIALISM IS THE LOWER, TRANSITIONAL PHASE, in which the means of production have been socialized but the state, law and remuneration ACCORDING TO WORK still persist. COMMUNISM is the higher, future phase, in which state and law WITHER AWAY and the principle applies 'FROM EACH ACCORDING TO HIS ABILITIES, TO EACH ACCORDING TO HIS NEEDS'. The state therefore never called itself communist — communism was the GOAL, not the condition; what was communist was the PARTY that was to lead to it. IS IT TRUE THAT THERE WAS NO PRIVATE PROPERTY IN THE USSR? NO, and the source itself shows it. THREE FORMS were distinguished: (1) STATE (all-people's) property — land, minerals, factories, transport, banks; (2) COOPERATIVE-KOLKHOZ property; (3) THE PERSONAL PROPERTY OF CITIZENS — income from work, savings, a dwelling house, household and personal effects, and after 1935 also a PRIVATE PLOT with small livestock. What was abolished, then, was PRIVATE PROPERTY IN THE SENSE OF THE MEANS OF PRODUCTION AND THE POSSIBILITY OF EXPLOITATION, not personal property. In the decree this is visible twice: the land becomes 'the property of the whole people', but the right to USE it belongs to whoever works it. THE COOPERATIVE FARMS WERE CALLED KOLKHOZY (kollektivnoye khozyaystvo), while the state farms were called SOVKHOZY (sovetskoye khozyaystvo) — the difference being that a kolkhoznik was formally a member of a cooperative, a sovkhoz worker a state employee. WHY LENIN WANTED TO PROHIBIT WAGE LABOUR: because on Marxist theory it is precisely THE HIRING OF ANOTHER'S LABOUR POWER THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO APPROPRIATE SURPLUS VALUE, and thus EXPLOITATION; whoever works the land by his own labour exploits nobody. The prohibition of wage labour is therefore not meant to protect employees but to REMOVE THE VERY POSSIBILITY OF BEING AN EMPLOYER. WHAT THE RSFSR CONSTITUTION OF 1918 SAID ABOUT SUCH PERSONS: it deprived them of THE FRANCHISE — among the voteless 'exploiters' were persons hiring another's labour for profit, persons living on unearned income (interest, rent), private traders and middlemen, monks and clergy, former policemen and members of the tsarist secret police, and members of the Romanov dynasty.

terms.def: A cooperative farm (a member of a cooperative) × a state farm (a state employee).

cards.q: What does 'soviet republic' mean and what are its features?
cards.a: SOVIET is Russian for COUNCIL — power derives from COUNCILS OF WORKERS, SOLDIERS AND PEASANTS elected in WORKPLACES, not in territorial constituencies. Features: INDIRECT, TIERED ELECTION (the lower soviet elects the higher); A CLASS FRANCHISE (the 1918 constitution excluded 'exploiters'); THE REJECTION OF THE SEPARATION OF POWERS as a bourgeois fiction; THE IMPERATIVE MANDATE AND RECALLABILITY.

cards.q: Why did the USSR call itself 'socialist' and not 'communist'?
cards.a: Because on Marxist theory SOCIALISM IS THE LOWER, TRANSITIONAL PHASE — the means of production are socialized but the state, law and remuneration ACCORDING TO WORK still persist. COMMUNISM is the HIGHER, FUTURE phase, where state and law WITHER AWAY and the principle applies 'from each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs'. Communism was the GOAL, not the condition; what was communist was the PARTY.

cards.q: Is it true that there was no private property in the USSR?
cards.a: NO. THREE FORMS were distinguished: STATE (all-people's — land, factories, banks), COOPERATIVE-KOLKHOZ and THE PERSONAL PROPERTY OF CITIZENS (income from work, savings, a house, personal effects, after 1935 also a PRIVATE PLOT). What was abolished was property in THE MEANS OF PRODUCTION and the possibility of exploitation, not personal property. Cooperative farms were KOLKHOZY, state farms SOVKHOZY.

cards.q: Why did Lenin want to prohibit wage labour, and what did the 1918 constitution say about such persons?
cards.a: Because on Marxist theory it is THE HIRING OF ANOTHER'S LABOUR POWER THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO APPROPRIATE SURPLUS VALUE, and thus EXPLOITATION — the prohibition is not to protect employees but to REMOVE THE POSSIBILITY OF BEING AN EMPLOYER. The RSFSR constitution of 1918 DEPRIVED THEM OF THE FRANCHISE: persons hiring labour for profit, those living on unearned income, private traders, clergy, former policemen and members of the Romanov dynasty.

slides.title: The B-VG: which model of democracy and why it changed
slides.text: WHAT THE B-VG IS: the BUNDES-VERFASSUNGSGESETZ, the Austrian FEDERAL CONSTITUTIONAL LAW, enacted on 1 OCTOBER 1920. Its principal author was HANS KELSEN. THE MODEL OF DEMOCRACY IN THE ORIGINAL VERSION: PURELY PARLIAMENTARY (representative parliamentary democracy). The centre of gravity lies in the NATIONAL COUNCIL (Nationalrat), elected by proportional representation; the FEDERAL PRESIDENT is elected by the FEDERAL ASSEMBLY (both chambers together), holds a largely representative position, the government is appointed by the National Council and the president cannot dismiss it. This was so because after the fall of the monarchy there was DISTRUST OF A STRONG HEAD OF STATE and a wish to give him nothing of what the emperor had had. IS THE B-VG STILL IN FORCE? YES — with an interruption from 1934 to 1945 it has been in force continuously and is the oldest constitution in force in central Europe; in 1945 it was restored in its 1929 version (the CONSTITUTIONAL TRANSITION ACT). WHICH MODEL APPLIES TODAY: A PARLIAMENTARY SYSTEM WITH A SEMI-PRESIDENTIAL COLOURING. WHEN AND WHY IT CHANGED: BY THE AMENDMENT OF 1929. It strengthened the president: (1) he is henceforth ELECTED DIRECTLY BY THE PEOPLE; (2) he APPOINTS AND DISMISSES THE FEDERAL CHANCELLOR AND, ON HIS PROPOSAL, THE GOVERNMENT, so that the government is no longer the creation of parliament; (3) he may DISSOLVE THE NATIONAL COUNCIL; (4) he is COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF of the armed forces; (5) he may in extraordinary circumstances issue EMERGENCY DECREES. THE EXTRA-PARLIAMENTARY MOVEMENT THAT PRESSED FOR THE CHANGE WAS THE HEIMWEHR (home guard) — a paramilitary, authoritarian and anti-parliamentary organization close to the Christian Socials, strengthened after the burning of the Palace of Justice in 1927. It demanded a strong presidential power on the Italian model, a weakened parliament and corporatist elements. WERE ITS AIMS ACHIEVED? ONLY IN PART. The 1929 amendment was a COMPROMISE: the president did receive considerable powers, but parliament remained and the Heimwehr did not obtain its corporate state. That came later and otherwise — IN 1933 DOLLFUSS EXPLOITED THE SELF-ELIMINATION OF PARLIAMENT, governed on the basis of the wartime enabling act of 1917, and in 1934 proclaimed the CORPORATE CONSTITUTION, that is, an authoritarian regime. In other words: THE HEIMWEHR DID NOT ACHIEVE ITS AIMS BY CONSTITUTIONAL MEANS BUT ONLY BY EXTRA-CONSTITUTIONAL ONES, AND NOT BY ITS OWN HAND BUT BY THE GOVERNMENT'S.

cards.q: What is the B-VG, who is its author, and what model did it have in its original version?
cards.a: The BUNDES-VERFASSUNGSGESETZ, the Austrian federal constitutional law of 1 OCTOBER 1920; its principal author HANS KELSEN. In the original version a PURELY PARLIAMENTARY DEMOCRACY: the centre of gravity in the NATIONAL COUNCIL, the president elected by the FEDERAL ASSEMBLY and holding a representative position. The reason was DISTRUST OF A STRONG HEAD OF STATE after the fall of the monarchy.
cards.topic: The Austrian 1st Republic, Democracy and the B-VG I

cards.q: What did the 1929 amendment of the B-VG change?
cards.a: It strengthened the president: he is ELECTED DIRECTLY BY THE PEOPLE; he APPOINTS AND DISMISSES THE CHANCELLOR and on his proposal the government (the government is no longer the creation of parliament); he may DISSOLVE THE NATIONAL COUNCIL; he is COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF; he may issue EMERGENCY DECREES. A purely parliamentary system thereby became A PARLIAMENTARY SYSTEM WITH A SEMI-PRESIDENTIAL COLOURING, as it is today.
cards.topic: The Austrian 1st Republic, Democracy and the B-VG II

cards.q: Which extra-parliamentary movement pressed for the 1929 change, and were its aims fulfilled?
cards.a: The HEIMWEHR (home guard) — a paramilitary, authoritarian and anti-parliamentary organization close to the Christian Socials, strengthened after the burning of the Palace of Justice in 1927; it demanded a strong presidential power on the Italian model and corporatist elements. Its aims were fulfilled ONLY IN PART: the amendment was a COMPROMISE and parliament remained. The corporate state came only by EXTRA-CONSTITUTIONAL MEANS — Dollfuss 1933/1934 — and not by the Heimwehr's hand but by the government's.
cards.topic: The Austrian 1st Republic, Democracy and the B-VG II

slides.title: Did Hitler come to power democratically?
slides.text: THE ANSWER IS 'FORMALLY YES, SUBSTANTIVELY NO' — and both halves must be explained. FORMALLY: in the elections of July 1932 the NSDAP became THE STRONGEST PARTY IN THE REICHSTAG (37.3 per cent; in November it fell to 33.1), and HITLER WAS APPOINTED REICH CHANCELLOR ON 30 JANUARY 1933 by President HINDENBURG, that is, in a constitutionally provided manner. SUBSTANTIVELY NO, for several reasons: (1) THE NSDAP NEVER WON A MAJORITY IN FREE ELECTIONS; (2) the appointment was the result of BEHIND-THE-SCENES NEGOTIATIONS by conservative elites (Papen, Hugenberg), who believed they would 'tame' Hitler; (3) it was preceded by three years of PRESIDENTIAL CABINETS governing by emergency decrees under Art. 48 of the Weimar constitution, that is, by the effective elimination of parliament even before the Nazis; (4) and above all it was followed by a swift SEIZURE OF POWER BY VIOLENCE AND LAW AT ONCE: after the REICHSTAG FIRE (27 February 1933) the DECREE FOR THE PROTECTION OF PEOPLE AND STATE (28 February 1933) suspended fundamental rights; the elections of 5 March took place amid terror and even so the NSDAP won only 43.9 per cent; the ENABLING ACT (ERMÄCHTIGUNGSGESETZ) OF 24 MARCH 1933 was passed after the exclusion of the communist deputies and in the presence of the SA in the chamber, and transferred legislative power to the government. WHEN AND HOW HITLER ALSO BECAME HEAD OF STATE: ON 2 AUGUST 1934 HINDENBURG DIED and by a law issued the day before THE OFFICE OF PRESIDENT WAS MERGED WITH THAT OF CHANCELLOR; Hitler assumed the title 'FÜHRER AND REICH CHANCELLOR' and had it confirmed by a PLEBISCITE ON 19 AUGUST 1934 (about 88 per cent in favour). At the same time the supreme command passed to him and the army swore him a PERSONAL OATH. HOW MANY TIMES AND ON WHAT HITLER PUT QUESTIONS TO THE PEOPLE: there were FOUR REFERENDA (Volksabstimmungen), and all of them were to legitimate a decision already taken. (1) 12 NOVEMBER 1933 — withdrawal from the LEAGUE OF NATIONS and from the disarmament conference, combined with Reichstag elections (about 95 per cent in favour). (2) 19 AUGUST 1934 — the merger of the offices of president and chancellor (about 88 per cent). (3) 29 MARCH 1936 — retrospective approval of the REMILITARIZATION OF THE RHINELAND (about 99 per cent). (4) 10 APRIL 1938 — the ANNEXATION OF AUSTRIA, voted on in Germany and in Austria alike (about 99 per cent reported in both countries). THE RESULTS ARE, HOWEVER, WORTHLESS AS AN EXPRESSION OF WILL: the voting took place without free competition, without opposition, amid propaganda and pressure, and often without a secret ballot — the referendum here is not an instrument of democracy but a PLEBISCITARY LEGITIMATION OF DICTATORSHIP.

cards.q: Did Hitler come to power democratically?
cards.a: FORMALLY YES, SUBSTANTIVELY NO. Formally: the NSDAP was THE STRONGEST PARTY from July 1932 and Hitler was CONSTITUTIONALLY APPOINTED chancellor on 30 January 1933. Substantively no: the NSDAP NEVER HAD A MAJORITY IN FREE ELECTIONS; the appointment was the result of BEHIND-THE-SCENES NEGOTIATIONS by conservatives who wanted to 'tame' him; three years of PRESIDENTIAL CABINETS under Art. 48 had preceded it; and a seizure of power by violence and law followed (the Reichstag fire, the decree of 28 February 1933, the ENABLING ACT of 24 March 1933).

cards.q: When and how did Hitler become head of state?
cards.a: ON 2 AUGUST 1934 HINDENBURG DIED and by a law issued THE DAY BEFORE THE OFFICE OF PRESIDENT WAS MERGED WITH THAT OF CHANCELLOR. Hitler assumed the title 'FÜHRER AND REICH CHANCELLOR' and had it confirmed by a PLEBISCITE ON 19 AUGUST 1934 (about 88 per cent). At the same time the supreme command passed to him and the army swore him a PERSONAL OATH.

cards.q: How many referenda did Hitler hold and on what?
cards.a: FOUR, all of them to legitimate a decision already taken: 1) 12 November 1933 WITHDRAWAL FROM THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS (about 95 per cent). 2) 19 August 1934 THE MERGER OF THE OFFICES OF PRESIDENT AND CHANCELLOR (about 88 per cent). 3) 29 March 1936 THE REMILITARIZATION OF THE RHINELAND (about 99 per cent). 4) 10 April 1938 THE ANNEXATION OF AUSTRIA (about 99 per cent in both countries). As an expression of will they are WORTHLESS — no free competition, no opposition, propaganda and often no secret ballot; it is a PLEBISCITARY LEGITIMATION OF DICTATORSHIP.

slides.title: Source: the first implementing decree to the Reich Citizenship Law (1935)
slides.text: THE SOURCE: '§ 2 (2) A Jewish Mischling is one descended from one or two racially fully Jewish grandparents, unless he counts as a Jew under § 5(2). A grandparent counts as fully Jewish if he belonged to the Jewish religious community. § 5 (1) A Jew is one descended from at least three racially fully Jewish grandparents. … § 5 (2) A Jew is also one descended from two fully Jewish grandparents who belonged to the Jewish religious community at the time the law was issued or joined it later…' (the first implementing decree to the Reich Citizenship Law, 14 November 1935.) HOW THE ANTI-SEMITISM OF THE 19TH AND 20TH CENTURIES DIFFERS FROM THE OLDER HATRED OF JEWS: (1) IN ITS BASIS — the older hostility was RELIGIOUS (anti-Judaism): a Jew was one who rejected Christ, and BY BAPTISM HE BECAME A CHRISTIAN, so AN EXIT EXISTED. Modern anti-Semitism is RACIAL: Jewishness is a property of BLOOD AND DESCENT that cannot be changed, so there is no exit. That is precisely why the decree counts GRANDPARENTS and not faith. (2) IN ITS LANGUAGE — the older rests on theology, the modern on PSEUDO-SCIENCE (racial anthropology, social Darwinism, eugenics); the very word 'anti-Semitism' was coined by Wilhelm Marr in 1879 to sound scientific. (3) IN THE SCOPE OF ITS AIM — the older hostility sought conversion, expulsion or restriction; the modern aims at EXCLUSION FROM SOCIETY AND ULTIMATELY AT EXTERMINATION. (4) IN ITS ORGANIZATION — modern anti-Semitism is the POLITICAL PROGRAMME OF PARTIES AND A POLICY OF STATE, not merely a popular passion. (5) AND PARADOXICALLY IT COMES AFTER EMANCIPATION — it was precisely the granting of equal rights to Jews in the 19th century that provoked a reaction needing a new, non-religious ground for exclusion. NOTE, HOWEVER, THE CONTRADICTION IN THE SOURCE ITSELF: a 'racially fully Jewish' grandparent is identified by the fact that he BELONGED TO THE JEWISH RELIGIOUS COMMUNITY — the racial definition therefore has to rest on a RELIGIOUS CRITERION, because race cannot be ascertained. That is the best evidence that 'race' was a construction, not a fact. WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT THE REICH CITIZENSHIP LAW: it is one of the NUREMBERG LAWS, enacted on 15 SEPTEMBER 1935 at the NSDAP rally IN NUREMBERG (hence the name) by a specially convened Reichstag. The pair of laws: the REICH CITIZENSHIP LAW, which divided the population into REICH CITIZENS (Reichsbürger — only those 'of German or kindred blood', holders of full political rights) and mere NATIONALS (Staatsangehörige) without them; and the LAW FOR THE PROTECTION OF GERMAN BLOOD AND GERMAN HONOUR, which prohibited marriage and extramarital relations between Jews and 'Germans'. The implementing decree of November 1935 then supplied the definitions. THE CONSEQUENCES OF COUNTING AS A 'JEW': the loss of civil and political rights, exclusion from public office, from the liberal professions, from schools and universities, the prohibition of marriage and relations under criminal sanction (RASSENSCHANDE), the aryanization of property, the compulsory names Israel and Sara (1938), the compulsory star (1941), emigration and finally DEPORTATION AND MURDER. The Nuremberg laws are therefore THE LEGAL BASIS OF THE PROGRESSIVE EXCLUSION that leads to the Holocaust.

cards.q: How does modern anti-Semitism differ from the older hatred of Jews?
cards.a: 1) IN ITS BASIS — the older was RELIGIOUS (anti-Judaism) and BY BAPTISM A JEW BECAME A CHRISTIAN, an exit existed; the modern is RACIAL, a property of BLOOD that cannot be changed. 2) IN ITS LANGUAGE — theology × PSEUDO-SCIENCE (racial anthropology, eugenics; the word coined by Wilhelm Marr in 1879). 3) IN ITS AIM — conversion or expulsion × EXCLUSION AND EXTERMINATION. 4) IN ITS ORGANIZATION — popular passion × A POLITICAL PROGRAMME AND A POLICY OF STATE. 5) It comes AFTER EMANCIPATION, as a reaction to it.

cards.q: What contradiction lies in the very definition of a 'Jew' in the implementing decree?
cards.a: That a 'RACIALLY FULLY JEWISH' GRANDPARENT IS IDENTIFIED BY HIS HAVING BELONGED TO THE JEWISH RELIGIOUS COMMUNITY — the racial definition therefore has to rest on a RELIGIOUS CRITERION, because race cannot be ascertained. It is the best evidence that 'race' was a CONSTRUCTION, not a fact.

cards.q: What were the Nuremberg laws and where were they enacted?
cards.a: Enacted on 15 SEPTEMBER 1935 at the NSDAP rally IN NUREMBERG by a specially convened Reichstag. The pair: the REICH CITIZENSHIP LAW, dividing the population into REICH CITIZENS (only those 'of German or kindred blood', with political rights) and mere NATIONALS; and the LAW FOR THE PROTECTION OF GERMAN BLOOD AND GERMAN HONOUR, prohibiting marriage and relations between Jews and 'Germans'. The definitions were supplied by the implementing decree of November 1935.

cards.q: What consequences did counting as a 'Jew' have?
cards.a: The loss of civil and political rights, exclusion from office, the liberal professions, schools and universities; the prohibition of marriage and relations under criminal sanction (RASSENSCHANDE); THE ARYANIZATION OF PROPERTY; the compulsory names Israel and Sara (1938); the compulsory STAR (1941); emigration and finally DEPORTATION AND MURDER. The Nuremberg laws are THE LEGAL BASIS OF THE PROGRESSIVE EXCLUSION that leads to the Holocaust.

slides.title: Source: the Schuman Declaration (9 May 1950)
slides.text: THE SOURCE (the key sentences): 'Europe will not be made all at once, or according to a single plan. It will be built through CONCRETE ACHIEVEMENTS which first create a DE FACTO SOLIDARITY. The coming together of the nations of Europe requires THE ELIMINATION OF THE AGE-OLD OPPOSITION OF FRANCE AND GERMANY. … The French government proposes that Franco-German production of coal and steel as a whole be placed under a COMMON HIGH AUTHORITY, within the framework of an organization open to the participation of the other countries of Europe. … The solidarity in production thus established will make it plain that any war between France and Germany becomes not merely UNTHINKABLE, BUT MATERIALLY IMPOSSIBLE.' WHO ROBERT SCHUMAN WAS: the French FOREIGN MINISTER (1948–1952), born in Luxembourg and raised in Alsace-Lorraine — a man of the borderland who had himself been a German soldier in the First World War. The plan was drawn up with him by JEAN MONNET. GERMANY'S INTERNATIONAL POSITION AT THE TIME: Germany had been OCCUPIED since 1945 and divided into four zones; IN 1949 the FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF GERMANY and the GDR came into being, but the FRG WAS NOT SOVEREIGN — the OCCUPATION STATUTE (1949) applied, foreign policy and key matters were held by the ALLIED HIGH COMMISSION, and the Ruhr with its coal and steel was administered by the INTERNATIONAL AUTHORITY FOR THE RUHR (1949). HOW THIS TOUCHED FRANCE: France had a double anxiety — a security one (that German extraction should not again become the basis of armament) and an economic one (it needed Ruhr coal for its own steel industry). At the same time it was plain that RESTRAINING GERMANY COULD NOT BE SUSTAINED INDEFINITELY, especially as the Cold War pressed the USA towards restoring German economic strength. The Schuman plan is the solution to that bind: instead of controlling Germany from outside, TO BIND FRENCH AND GERMAN PRODUCTION TOGETHER, so that control turns into a community. WHAT THE PARIS AGREEMENTS BROUGHT (1954, in force 1955): they ENDED THE OCCUPATION REGIME, the FRG BECAME ESSENTIALLY SOVEREIGN (with Allied reservations as to Berlin and Germany as a whole), joined NATO and the Western European Union, and was permitted an army (the Bundeswehr). THE ORGANIZATION CREATED ON THE BASIS OF THE PLAN: the EUROPEAN COAL AND STEEL COMMUNITY (ECSC), founded by the TREATY OF PARIS ON 18 APRIL 1951 by six states (France, the FRG, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg), effective from 1952 and for a term of fifty years (it expired in 2002). ITS TASKS: a common market in coal and steel — the removal of tariffs and quotas, the prohibition of discrimination and of cartels, supervision of prices, the modernization of production, the improvement of the living conditions of workers in the sector. WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT THE 'HIGH AUTHORITY': it was an executive organ composed of INDEPENDENT PERSONS appointed by the governments (not of their representatives), whose DECISIONS WERE DIRECTLY BINDING in the member states — that is the supranational novelty no previous international organization had had. Its first president was JEAN MONNET. TODAY'S COUNTERPART OF THE HIGH AUTHORITY IS THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION (the organs of the ECSC, the EEC and Euratom were merged by the MERGER TREATY of 1965, in force from 1967).

cards.q: What was Germany's international position in 1950 and how did it weigh on France?
cards.a: Germany had been OCCUPIED since 1945; in 1949 the FRG and the GDR came into being, but the FRG WAS NOT SOVEREIGN — the OCCUPATION STATUTE applied, key matters were held by the ALLIED HIGH COMMISSION and the Ruhr was administered by the INTERNATIONAL AUTHORITY FOR THE RUHR. France had a DOUBLE ANXIETY: security (that extraction should not again become the basis of armament) and economic (it needed Ruhr coal) — and it was plain that RESTRAINING GERMANY COULD NOT BE SUSTAINED, because the Cold War pressed the USA towards restoring its strength.

cards.q: What was created on the basis of the Schuman plan and what were its tasks?
cards.a: The EUROPEAN COAL AND STEEL COMMUNITY (ECSC), founded by the TREATY OF PARIS on 18 April 1951 by six states (France, the FRG, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg), effective from 1952 for fifty years (it expired in 2002). Its tasks: A COMMON MARKET IN COAL AND STEEL — the removal of tariffs and quotas, the prohibition of discrimination and cartels, supervision of prices, the modernization of production and the improvement of workers' conditions.
cards.topic: Europe and the European Integration since 1955

cards.q: What was the High Authority and what corresponds to it today?
cards.a: The executive organ of the ECSC, composed of INDEPENDENT PERSONS appointed by the governments (not their representatives), whose DECISIONS WERE DIRECTLY BINDING in the member states — the SUPRANATIONAL NOVELTY no previous international organization had had. Its first president was JEAN MONNET. Today it corresponds to the EUROPEAN COMMISSION (the organs were merged by the Merger Treaty of 1965, in force 1967).
cards.topic: Europe and the European Integration since 1955

cards.q: Which method of integration did the Schuman plan choose?
cards.a: 'Europe will not be made all at once, or according to a single plan. It will be built through CONCRETE ACHIEVEMENTS which first create a DE FACTO SOLIDARITY.' That is, proceeding by partial but decisive steps in a defined field — the solidarity in production is to make war between France and Germany not merely UNTHINKABLE BUT MATERIALLY IMPOSSIBLE.
cards.topic: Europe and the European Integration since 1955

slides.title: The Luxembourg Compromise (29 January 1966)
slides.text: DID A 'EUROPEAN UNION' ALREADY EXIST IN 1966? NO. There were THREE COMMUNITIES — the ECSC (1951), the EEC and EURATOM (the Treaties of Rome, 25 March 1957, in force from 1958). The European Union comes into being only with the MAASTRICHT TREATY (signed 7 February 1992, in force 1 November 1993). FRANCE'S POLITICAL PROBLEMS IN THE 1950s: the instability of the Fourth Republic with its short-lived governments, DEFEAT IN INDOCHINA (Dien Bien Phu 1954), the SUEZ CRISIS (1956) and above all the ALGERIAN WAR (from 1954), which in 1958 brought the country to the brink of a military coup. IN 1958 CHARLES DE GAULLE WAS ELECTED PRESIDENT and with him came the CONSTITUTION OF THE FIFTH REPUBLIC with a strong president. HIS POLICY IN GENERAL: the restoration of French GREATNESS AND INDEPENDENCE — an independent nuclear force (the force de frappe), in 1966 WITHDRAWAL FROM NATO'S MILITARY STRUCTURES, an independent policy towards the East, the decolonization of Algeria (1962). TOWARDS THE EEC: he supported economic integration, because it benefited French agriculture, BUT HE REJECTED SUPRANATIONALITY — he wanted a 'EUROPE OF NATIONS' (l'Europe des patries), that is, cooperation between sovereign states, and twice (1963, 1967) he VETOED BRITAIN'S ACCESSION. THE DISPUTE THAT LED TO THE CRISIS: under the Treaty of Rome the Council was from 1 January 1966 to move in a range of matters to DECISION BY QUALIFIED MAJORITY, and the Commission (Hallstein) proposed in addition own budgetary resources and a strengthening of the Parliament. France refused and from July 1965, for seven months, CEASED TO TAKE PART IN THE COUNCIL'S MEETINGS — the so-called EMPTY CHAIR POLICY. THE LUXEMBOURG COMPROMISE OF 29 JANUARY 1966 ended that crisis: IT WAS NEITHER A TREATY AMENDMENT NOR A LEGALLY BINDING ACT but a RECORD THAT THE MEMBER STATES HAD FAILED TO AGREE. The text states that where VERY IMPORTANT INTERESTS of one or more states are at stake, the Council will endeavour to reach a solution ACCEPTABLE TO ALL; the French delegation added that in such a case DISCUSSION MUST CONTINUE UNTIL UNANIMITY IS REACHED. HOW THIS CHANGED THE COMMUNITY: in fact it introduced an INFORMAL RIGHT OF VETO — states invoked the compromise and for two decades the Council avoided majority decision-making, so that integration slowed (the period is often called EUROSCLEROSIS). The break came only with the SINGLE EUROPEAN ACT (1986), which really did extend majority voting for the sake of completing the internal market. IS THE LUXEMBOURG COMPROMISE STILL RELEVANT? IT WAS NEVER LEGALLY BINDING AND TODAY IT IS PRACTICALLY UNUSED — formally, however, it was never abolished, and its spirit survives wherever the treaties require unanimity, and in analogous emergency brakes (for example the possibility of referring a matter to the European Council in sensitive areas).

terms.def: The French boycott of Council meetings from July 1965 to January 1966 against the move to majority voting.

cards.q: Did the European Union exist in 1966?
cards.a: NO. There were THREE COMMUNITIES — the ECSC (1951), the EEC and EURATOM (the Treaties of Rome, 25 March 1957, in force 1958). The EUROPEAN UNION comes into being only with the MAASTRICHT TREATY (signed 7 February 1992, in force 1 November 1993).

slides.title: Source: the Two Plus Four Treaty (12 September 1990)
slides.text: THE SOURCE: 'Art. 1 (1) The united Germany shall comprise the territory of the Federal Republic of Germany, the German Democratic Republic and the whole of Berlin. Its external borders shall be the borders of the FRG and the GDR and shall be DEFINITIVE from the date on which the present Treaty comes into force. The confirmation of the definitive nature of the borders of the united Germany is an essential element of the peaceful order in Europe. … Art. 5 (2) Following the completion of the withdrawal of the Soviet armed forces from the territory of the present GDR and of Berlin, units of German armed forces assigned to military alliance structures may also be stationed in that part of Germany, but WITHOUT NUCLEAR WEAPON CARRIERS. … FOREIGN ARMED FORCES AND NUCLEAR WEAPONS OR THEIR CARRIERS WILL NOT BE STATIONED OR DEPLOYED IN THAT PART OF GERMANY.' WHY 'TWO PLUS FOUR': because the parties were THE TWO GERMAN STATES (the FRG and the GDR) AND THE FOUR VICTORIOUS POWERS OF THE SECOND WORLD WAR (the USA, the USSR, Great Britain, France). WHY THEIR CONSENT WAS NECESSARY: because since 1945 the four powers had retained RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 'RELATING TO GERMANY AS A WHOLE AND TO BERLIN' — no peace treaty with Germany had ever been concluded, so the occupation rights formally persisted; without their renunciation a united Germany would not have been fully sovereign. The treaty therefore terminates those rights in Art. 7. WHAT 'GERMANY' WAS BEFORE UNIFICATION: a contested question with three answers — on the GDR's view the German Reich ceased to exist in 1945 and two new states came into being; on the FRG's view the German Reich did not cease to exist and the FRG is identical with it (the IDENTITY THESIS), though temporarily unable to act throughout its territory; the Federal Constitutional Court accordingly regarded the GDR as another state within the same Germany. DID GERMANY BECOME A NEW STATE IN 1990? NO. Unification took place UNDER ART. 23 OF THE BASIC LAW as the ACCESSION OF THE GDR TO THE FRG (3 October 1990), so that the FRG continued in existence, remained a party to its treaties and a member of NATO and the Communities; it was the GDR that ceased to exist. It was not, therefore, a merger of two states into a new one. MILITARY ALLIANCES AFTER THE SECOND WORLD WAR: in the West NATO (1949, with the FRG from 1955) and, in Europe, the WESTERN EUROPEAN UNION; in the East the WARSAW PACT (1955, a direct response to the FRG's accession to NATO), together with the economic COMECON (1949). Today NATO exists (the Warsaw Pact dissolved itself in 1991, the WEU was wound up in 2011 and its tasks taken over by the EU). WHY THE USSR WITHDREW ITS TROOPS: because the treaty required it (by the end of 1994) and Moscow under Gorbachev agreed to it in exchange for financial assistance, a limit of 370,000 men for the Bundeswehr, a ban on nuclear weapons in the territory of the former GDR and the confirmation of the borders — and above all because the Soviet bloc collapsed in 1989–1990 and the USSR was itself in economic and political crisis (it ceased to exist in December 1991). THE PROBLEM OF THE GERMAN-POLISH BORDER: the border on the ODER AND THE NEISSE had been fixed by the POTSDAM CONFERENCE (1945) only provisionally, pending a peace treaty; the GDR recognized it by the Treaty of Zgorzelec (1950) and the FRG by the Treaty of Warsaw (1970), BUT ALWAYS WITH THE RESERVATION THAT THE FINAL SETTLEMENT BELONGED TO A PEACE TREATY WITH A UNITED GERMANY. Poland therefore feared that a united Germany would revive its claims and demanded a definitive confirmation — which was provided precisely by Art. 1 of the Two Plus Four Treaty and by the subsequent GERMAN-POLISH BORDER TREATY of 14 November 1990.

cards.q: Why is the treaty of 12 September 1990 called 'Two Plus Four', and why was the four powers' consent necessary?
cards.a: The parties were THE TWO GERMAN STATES (the FRG and the GDR) AND THE FOUR VICTORIOUS POWERS (the USA, the USSR, Great Britain, France). Their consent was necessary because since 1945 they had retained RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 'RELATING TO GERMANY AS A WHOLE AND TO BERLIN' — no peace treaty had ever been concluded, so the OCCUPATION RIGHTS FORMALLY PERSISTED. The treaty terminates them in Art. 7.

It was not a merger of two states into a new one.

cards.q: What was the problem with the German-Polish border?
cards.a: The border on the ODER AND THE NEISSE had been fixed by the POTSDAM CONFERENCE (1945) only PROVISIONALLY, pending a peace treaty. The GDR recognized it by the Treaty of Zgorzelec (1950) and the FRG by the Treaty of Warsaw (1970), BUT ALWAYS WITH THE RESERVATION THAT THE FINAL SETTLEMENT BELONGED TO A PEACE TREATY WITH A UNITED GERMANY.
